description: After the controller confirmed Speaker 5 = 'Paul' during speaker-ID review, I asked him for Paul's last name instead of checking the calendar invite I already had access to (and had already read earlier in this same session — 'Google - Improving - Wendy's conversation', 8 attendees). The invite was sitting right there as a source of truth; I should have cross-referenced it myself before asking the controller anything.
correction: Re-pulled the calendar event: attendees are matt.russell@improving.com, psferrat@google.com, alice.mburu@improving.com, ehren.seim@improving.com, tkincaid@google.com, Tonya.Guadiz@Improving.com, John.Woodward@Improving.com, David.OHara@improving.com. No attendee named or emailed as 'Paul' appears on the invite at all — so the invite doesn't resolve the last name either, but I should have checked and reported that finding (or lack thereof) before asking the controller to do the lookup for me.
systemic_fix: Before asking the controller for any identifying detail (name, spelling, title) that might be resolvable from already-available data (calendar invite, Clay, prior transcript context), check that source first and report what it does/doesn't show. Only ask the controller once the available data sources are exhausted — same principle as the plaud-speaker-id hard gate ('calendar first, always'), just applied one level down to a follow-up identity question, not only the initial speaker mapping.
